conviction_note: Honest zero: the only company-specific lead (a Q4 fuel-margin tailwind read off Casey's, Murphy USA and the EIA price path) was already in Oppenheimer's 2026-09-16 preview as 'excess fuel profits' Costco may reinvest. The swing factor, the IEEPA refund (~$1.5B per Evercore, one-third received by 5 Aug, returned to members through price cuts), is fully in the wire. On a name that fell after 7 of its last 10 prints, neither is worth a size.
bar: Q4 FY26 EPS $6.55 consensus (TipRanks https://www.tipranks.com/news/costco-cost-reports-q4-earnings-on-sept-24-heres-what-analysts-expect and Yahoo/Barchart https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/expect-costco-wholesales-q4-2026-134037110.html agree; the sweep cites $6.48-6.54 elsewhere, and Oppenheimer's own number is $6.34). Revenue is effectively pre-reported: Q4 net sales were $93.9B per the 2026-09-02 August sales release (https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-August-Sales-Results/default.aspx). Costco gives no guidance.

outside_window.finding: Special dividend: cash is approaching $20B and Evercore sees 'growing potential' within a year, but does not expect one this week. Costco has never announced a special dividend with a September Q4 print; the last was announced in December 2023. Undated, so it is not sized into the window.

FY27 reinvestment of IEEPA tariff refunds into lower prices. Oppenheimer flags profit headwinds from that reinvestment in the coming fiscal year. It would reach the stock through commentary on the call, but the P&L effect lands after the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filing list since 2026-05-01 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000909832&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40): the 8-K of 07-08 is the June sales release plus the regular $1.47 dividend; there is a routine S-3ASR shelf on 06-03, one EVP Form 3 on 09-10 (William Richard Wilcox) and routine Form 4s and 144s. No quiet 8-K.

Q3 FY26 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000909832/000090983226000051/cost-20260510.htm): no tariff-refund receivable and no accrual for the four consumer class actions; the only accounting change is the digitally-enabled comps definition. No wording change that points at the Q4 print.

Tariff refunds: the Aug 5 filing in Stockov v. Costco (N.D. Ill. 1:26-cv-02734) says about one-third of refunds were received and returned through lower prices (https://www.cfodive.com/news/costco-fights-customers-tariff-suit-refunds-flow/828644/, 2026-08-24). No dollar figure is disclosed. Evercore ($1.5B), RBC and Oppenheimer all model it, so it is in the wire.

Fuel margin: Casey's May-Jul fuel margin was 47.8 cpg against 41.0 (https://investor.caseys.com/news-releases/news-release-details/caseys-announces-first-quarter-results-3, 2026-09-08). Murphy USA's Q2 fuel contribution was 40.6 cpg against 32.0 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001573516/000157351626000164/exh991_06302026er.htm). The EIA regular price peaked at $4.48 in May, then fell to $3.93-3.97 in Jun-Jul and rose to $4.07 in Aug (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?f=W&n=PET&s=EMM_EPMR_PTE_NUS_DPG). All of that points to wide gas margins in Costco's Q4, but Costco said on the Q3 call that it widens price gaps (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/28/costco-cost-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/), and Oppenheimer's preview already discusses 'excess fuel profits' being reinvested (https://www.tipranks.com/news/cost-stock-is-the-options-market-overestimating-costcos-q4-post-earnings-reaction). Dropped after LESSONS.

Membership: US/Canada renewal was 92.2% (+10bp sequentially) and worldwide 89.7% at Q3. The digital-signup and Groupon renewal drag is company-disclosed and covered by Zacks. No app-store or forum signal found.
Labor cost: the March 2026 $1/hr Teamsters step is contractual and already known.
Special dividend: covered by TipRanks, Evercore and Oppenheimer; not expected this week (outside_window).
baseline_tension: Nothing found cuts against the baseline. The skew leans up, the stock has derated 18% from its high, and the sell-side debate (headline refund gain against core margin mix) is fully in the wire, so the price already has what I found.
